comment: One place mapping real time to simulation time. Changing ticks_per_day changes pacing only; per-tick behaviour is unaffected.
pace_comment: ticks_per_day is set against the ground the trains actually cover. A tile is WorldConstants.TILE_METRES across, the shipped mine-to-works route is some 170 of them, and a loaded 4-4-0 covers one at the speed it is rated at: a leg measures 80 to 100 seconds of play at 1x and the first paid delivery nearer four. At 12 ticks a day a calendar month came round every 18 of those seconds, so a pit filled its platform to the ceiling and wasted everything above it long before one consist could clear a single load. 60 puts a month at 90 seconds, a little over one leg, which is the pace the industry output rates and the platform storages were sized for. Per-day quantities do not move with it: rates are divided by this number.

train.train_comment: acceleration and braking are changes of tiles-per-tick per tick, so they belong to the same scale as the speed they reach: 0.35 m/s^2 and 0.90 m/s^2 through WorldConstants.TILE_METRES at SimulationClock.TICK_RATE. Figures tuned for a faster-drawn consist brake a train to a dead stop on a gradient instead of slowing it.
